newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Former Afghan president starts mediation mission.
newsitem.headline: Former Afghan president starts mediation mission.

text.p: Former Afghan president Sibghatullah Mojadidi left Pakistan on Monday for a peace mission to the opposition-held north of Afghanistan, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

Mojadidi's spokesman, Waheed Ullah, told the Afghan Islamic Press that the ex-president had gone from the Pakistani border city of Peshawar to Dubai on his way to Tehran, from where he would fly to the opposition capital of Mazar-i-Sharif.

Mojadidi launched his mission, aimed at securing a ceasefire and an exchange of prisoners, after consulting the purist Islamic Taleban militia and ethnic Uzbek opposition leader General Abdul Malik, the spokesman said.
The Taleban want Malik to free hundreds of Taleban fighters captured in Mazar-i-Sharif last month.

The Taleban captives include some key leaders who had gone to Mazar-i-Sharif for talks with Malik, who had made a short-lived alliance with the Taleban against former opposition warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Malik turned on the Taleban at the end of May, linking up with a Shi'ite Moslem opposition faction to drive them from Mazar-i-Sharif after 15 hours of street fighting.

Taleban Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous, northern military commander Mullah Abdul Razzaq, central bank chief Mullah Ahsanullah, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Mullah Akhtar Mohammad Mansoor, High Council member Mullah Mohammad Siddiq are among those believed to be in Malik's hands.
Mojadidi was Afghanistan's first president for three months after Islamic mujahideen guerrillas took over Kabul from the pro-communist government of Najibullah in April 1992.
He was replaced by Burhanuddin Rabbani, whose government was driven from the Afghan capital by the Taleban in September.

The mainly ethnic Pashtun Taleban, trying to spread their austere version of Islamic law throughout Afghanistan, control more than two-thirds of the country but have failed to quell resistance from non-Pashtun opposition groups in the north.
